claims.title: Mechanism model
claims.statement: A parameter sweep and regression source are available for inspection.
assumptions: The authored geometric model is an adequate representation for the question being asked.
limitations: Computed geometry is not a measurement of an assembled mechanism.
Regression agreement does not establish physical model validity.
next_evidence: Independently reviewed model assumptions and an inert, instrumented physical comparison.

claims.title: Timing evidence
claims.statement: Timer source and a synthetic timing fixture exist; measured hardware jitter is unavailable.
assumptions: Fixture rows exercise report calculations only.
limitations: Synthetic values do not demonstrate timer, scheduler, or actuator behavior.
Twenty-one synthetic rows cannot establish a physical tail-latency bound.
next_evidence: Raw inert timing capture with instrument identity, sampling method, source revision, and uncertainty.
concerns: Historical wording described synthetic values as validating a hardware jitter requirement. That inference is unsupported.

claims.title: CAD generator software
claims.statement: Parametric generation code and regression tests are present.
assumptions: The selected CAD dependency versions and test environment are recorded by the execution workflow.
limitations: Test source is not an execution record.
Generating a CAD solid does not establish aerodynamic or structural performance.
next_evidence: Retained CI execution record and independently inspected exported geometry.

claims.title: Material mass accounting
claims.statement: Baseline and candidate mass rollups are calculated from authored material and volume assumptions.
assumptions: Part volumes, densities, and the included assembly scope are representative.
limitations: Calculated mass differences are not measured prototype savings.
Assembly additions and manufacturing variability require separate accounting.
next_evidence: Traceable as-built part masses and a reconciled assembly inventory.

claims.title: Stability model trace
claims.statement: Model input, implementation, and calculated output are available together.
assumptions: The simplified formulation and its input interpretation are applicable to the modeled case.
limitations: A calculated static margin does not establish dynamic stability or flight readiness.
Input revisions selected to match a target require independent justification.
next_evidence: Independent review of input provenance, model applicability, and uncertainty.

claims.title: Margin claim consistency
claims.statement: The historical note reports a 19% calculated margin against a stated requirement of at least 20%.
assumptions: The stated requirement and reported margin use the same definition and design point.
limitations: A positive margin does not establish satisfaction of a larger stated requirement.
No measured component characterization is included.
next_evidence: Reviewer reconciliation of the requirement, arithmetic, and acceptance test before asserting satisfaction.
concerns: The reported percentage is below the stated requirement.
The legacy test named for a 20% margin does not actually enforce that lower bound.

claims.title: Reliability evidence completeness
claims.statement: The committed CSV is a failure-only export with zero data rows, not a complete trial record.
assumptions: A reliability interpretation would require an explicit trial count, seed, model revision, and outcome definition.
limitations: An empty failure list cannot establish the number of trials executed.
Simulation outcomes do not measure physical reliability.
No empirical confidence bound is asserted by this review.
next_evidence: An independently reviewed run record with explicit denominator and complete provenance, followed by physical evidence for any hardware claim.
concerns: The historical 100% statement cannot be reconstructed from the committed CSV alone.

claims.title: Structural claim boundaries
claims.statement: Simplified laminate and hinge calculations exist; the material stiffness comparison is qualified by its own evidence note.
assumptions: Idealized material properties, layup, geometry, and load assumptions represent the modeled case.
limitations: Material modulus and component bending stiffness are different quantities.
An analytical factor of safety is not a qualification test.
Manufacturing defects and actual loads are unmeasured.
next_evidence: Independent reconciliation of material and component stiffness claims, with measured component characterization.
concerns: The original modulus output is below the comparison material; a thickness-compensation statement is not independent validation.
